platform: macOS 26.5 (25F71), arm64, Apple Silicon; debug build with the embedded frontend, isolated test mode (ADR 0003, macOS amendment), WKWebView driven through the test bridge (src-tauri/src/test_bridge.rs)
harness: node scripts/macos/m1-08-attachments.mjs --exe <exe> --port 9433 --base <tmp> --out-dir <dir> (scripts/macos/test-instance.mjs launch(), scripts/cdp-harness.mjs IPC trace)
method: page-built File objects through DataTransfer into the composer's <input type=file> (change) and the drop handler; DOM.setFileInputFiles is not served by the WKWebView bridge. The image is a 64x64 solid red PNG built by the harness, so the answer is checkable; the bytes in send_input's image part (IPC trace) are compared with it. Messages typed with Input.insertText and sent with a real Enter.

ninth-refused-empty-draft.error: You can attach up to 8 files with a written message (8 without).

eighth-refused-with-text.error: You can attach up to 7 files with a written message (8 without).

parts.text: What colour is the attached image? Answer with just the colour name in lower case.

unsent.text: Nine parts mv6h17en: eight images and this text.
unsent.error: send_input failed: inputParts cannot contain more than 8 parts

after-discard.composerText: Nine parts mv6h17en: eight images and this text.

limits: Files reach the page as page-built File objects (DataTransfer), not through the macOS open panel of <input type=file> nor a Finder drag: the bridge serves neither DOM.setFileInputFiles nor native drag and drop. The app's own intake (onChange/onDrop -> readAttachment) is what runs. Picking a file in the real open panel and dropping one from Finder remain for a session with Étienne.

After the refused 9-part send, Discard removes the unsent row but the composer still holds the 8 images and the text (recorded in after-discard): the message exists twice until then. Not data loss; logged for the backlog.

With an empty draft the over-limit copy reads 'You can attach up to 8 files with a written message (8 without)': the wording is meant for a non-empty draft (cross-platform copy defect, logged for the backlog).

Since 27/09 the UI counts the text as a part, so the 8-image + text wire refusal of the Windows record is reached by attaching 8 images with an empty draft, then typing: the UI does not re-check the cap when text is added after the files (logged for the backlog).
